name: Murder at the Manor
description: A guest lies dead at the manor. Each suspect was in a different room with a different motive. Work out whodunit.
clues: Heir goes with either Blackwood or Writing (but not both).
Either Blackwood goes with Writing, or Valet goes with Walking — but not both.
If Ashford goes with Writing, then Writing goes with Valet.
Either Blackwood goes with Writing or Valet goes with Blackwood.

hints.text: Suppose Heir didn't go with Writing — that hits a contradiction, so it does.
chain: Start by assuming Heir does not go with Writing.
From the clue “Heir goes with either Blackwood or Writing (but not both)” — Blackwood must go with Heir.
Blackwood goes with Heir, so it can't also go with Valet.
Blackwood goes with Heir, but Writing doesn't, so Blackwood doesn't go with Writing.
…but now the clue “Either Blackwood goes with Writing or Valet goes with Blackwood” can no longer hold — a contradiction.
